title: Oriental Rail Infrastructure Ltd - 531859 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Oriental Rail Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 29% YoY to INR172.5 crores, PAT up 44% to INR15.3 crores, with H1 order book at INR1,571 crores.
summary.overview: Consolidated Q2 FY27 revenue was INR172.5 crores (+29% YoY), EBITDA INR27.9 crores (+29%, 16.2% margin) and PAT INR15.3 crores (+44%). H1 revenue was INR310.1 crores (+23%), EBITDA INR48.8 crores (+35%) and PAT INR26.1 crores (+58%). Wagon output (subsidiary OFPL) rose 30% QoQ to 390 units, but was short of the 500 target because plant changes ran about 15 days late. Management guided to 600 wagons per quarter from Q3 and H2 revenue at least 25-30% above H1, while new initiatives (smart wagons, 25-ton bogie, leasing, coach refurbishment) are mostly pegged to FY28.

financial_highlights.change: Figure of around INR300 crores given on call was corrected

segments.name: Railway interiors and seats (parent)
segments.commentary: Current interior furnishing revenue about INR45-50 crores of the INR310 crores H1 base; management expects at least 100% growth over the next 4-5 quarters. Parent claims about 30% share of the organised seat and berth market, with 3,600 coach-set capacity.

segments.name: Freight wagons (OFPL, wholly owned)
segments.commentary: Produced 390 wagons in Q2 vs 300 in Q1 (+30% QoQ) against a 500 target; installed capacity 2,400 wagons a year; order book above 2,000 wagons, covering roughly three to four quarters.

segments.name: Consolidated order book
segments.commentary: About INR1,571 crores as of 21 Oct 2026, or 2.74x FY26 revenue. Management said H2 seat and berth revenue will be higher than H1 given longer-duration contracts.

guidance_outlook: Wagon output: at least 600 wagons per quarter from Q3 FY27, continuing in Q4; catch up the 390-wagon shortfall from Q2.
H2 FY27 revenue at least 25-30% above H1 (H1 INR310.1 crores), per management's reply to a question.
Production growth of at least 30-35% in Q3 over Q2.

Interior refurbishment: order book of at least INR100 crores plus by March 2027; target order inflow of about INR130 crores from INR400 crores of tenders quoted by December 2026, at a 30% strike rate.
Smart wagon order (RDSO tender, about 300-400 wagons, with HUM International): expected by mid-November 2026, with a conservative minimum of 200 units.
EBITDA margin expected to improve by about 6 percentage points relative to prior levels (for example 12-15% to 16-16.5%), per management's framing.
Capacity augmentation to 3,600 coach sets planned to start from April 2027; leasing entry from April 2027 onwards.
25-ton axle load bogie and gondola: RDSO design submission by December 2026; prototype and field trials in 6-9 months; regular supply orders from FY28.
capex_capacity: Wagon production: 390 units in Q2 vs 500 target; the shortfall was due to capital and technical changes on the plant completed about 15 days behind schedule.
Wagon capacity: installed capacity 2,400 wagons a year at OFPL; about 3,600 coach sets a year for seats and berths; four manufacturing units across about 100 acres.

Capacity augmentation planned to be finalised by February-March 2027 and implemented from April 2027. Land and permissions are already available, and the modern wagon design will be built in a new facility.
Backward integration: spring manufacturing in operation for about one year. Two or three more components are in discussion, with production expected from the middle of FY28.
Vande Bharat chair car seat order to be delivered by quarter ending June 2027; turnkey Vande Bharat furnishing readiness by January 2028.
demand_pricing: Management estimates Indian Railways needs about 35,000-40,000 wagons a year (about 20,000 replacement and 12,000-15,000 growth), against industry capacity of about 30,000-35,000. Management described this as its own estimate rather than a railway forecast.

Last large railway wagon tender was in 2023, covering about 80,000-90,000 wagons over three years. Management said timing of the next tender cannot be predicted, though visibility is 'definitely' there.
Interior furnishing market is about INR700-800 crores with three to four participants; management hopes to win about INR150 crores in the first one to two years, rising to about INR200 crores.

Steel prices rose sharply in the last quarter (Q2), including HR, stainless and spring steel; the company says price variation formulas in railway tenders largely cover the increase. Supply tie-ups and advance orders were placed.

Management said that Vande Bharat is a target and that private freight operators (Tata, Jindal) are a target for the modern wagon once RDSO-vetted; export discussions with a public sector network are at an early stage.

qa_highlights.question: Why were only 390 wagons produced against the 500 target, and what is the Q3 run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed technical and capital changes on the plant that finished about 15 days late. It expects to clear the 390 backlog and deliver about 500 plus 110 in Q3, and later said 600 per quarter from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Net debt as of 30 September and the inventory build-up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management first said around INR300 crores; the footnote corrects this to INR193.5 crores. Inventory rose because of advance steel buying amid volatile supply, and inventory should be under control by March 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Expected revenue run rate for H2 and EBITDA margin path?
qa_highlights.answer: H2 revenue should be at least 25-30% above H1. Management said price variation mechanisms limit raw-material downside, and margins should improve on higher utilisation and backward integration.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the smart wagon tender and the 25-ton bogie development?
qa_highlights.answer: The smart wagon financial bids are expected to open shortly, with orders by mid-November and a minimum of 200 units. The RDSO design submission is due by December 2026, with regular supply orders from FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Plans for wagon leasing and the impact of a railway tender delay?
qa_highlights.answer: Leasing entry is planned from April 2027. Average lease tenure is about 10 years (9-12). Management named railway leasing companies and private operators (GATX, Tata) as alternative buyers.

qa_highlights.question: Is any refurbishment order flow in place, and what margins apply?
qa_highlights.answer: Tenders of about INR150 crores are quoted against about two to three competitors, with a further INR200 crores pipeline. Management declined to disclose refurbishment EBITDA margins on the call, citing the investor presentation.

risks_watch: Execution: Q2 wagon output missed the 500 target. Q3 must reach 600 wagons as guided, and H2 revenue must be 25-30% above H1.
Working capital: short-term borrowings rose in H1 to fund inventory built up ahead of steel price moves; watch inventory days and whether they fall by March 2027.

Dependence on railway tenders: the order book covers about 3-4 quarters, and the next large railway wagon tender has no timeline. Leasing, HUM smart wagons and private operators are not yet revenue-generating.
Interior refurbishment: the INR150 crores of bids have not yet converted to orders; management target of about INR130 crores assumes a 30% strike rate.
Investor queries left open: net debt was misquoted on the call, and the INR50 crores loan and advance asset query was taken offline. Management also declined to comment on share price performance.
Steel price volatility: management says price variation clauses cover most of it, but the company will need to show margins holding in Q3 and Q4.
summary.management_tone: Confident and forward-looking on growth, order visibility and new products, but evasive on specifics: it declined to give order-book split, refurbishment margins, leasing IRR and ROCE, and the share price question. Several numbers were corrected or deferred to the investor presentation or offline follow-up.
key_quotes: Our consolidated order book stood at approximately INR1,571 crores as of October 21, 2026, representing 2.74x financial year '26 revenue.
We intend to go 600 from, it means at least about 600 from Q3, and that should continue in the Q4 also.
The volatility of the RM prices is sufficiently covered under the price variation formula, which are applicable on all wagon tenders, which is the major revenue component of the group right now.
H2 should be at least about 25% to 30% over H1.

adds.what: Capacity augmentation to 3,600 coach sets (seats and berths) at parent
New modern wagon facility (new design, land and permissions available)

growth.why: Management guides H2 FY27 revenue at least 25-30% above H1 (INR310.1 cr) and wagon output of at least 600/quarter from Q3, backed by a ~INR1,571 cr order book (2.74x FY26 revenue) and 2,000+ wagon order book, though the 3,600 coach-set augmentation and new facilities only start from April 2027 and Q2 wagons (390) missed the 500 target.
